note: BLOCKED ON INSTRUMENT RIGHTS (2026-09-10, batch_145) -- no ptacek2023_compact__items.csv written, nothing staged or uploaded. Instrument is the CompACT (Comprehensive assessment of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy processes; Francis, Dawson & Golijani-Moghaddam, 2016), administered here in Czech translation. The rights holder's own page -- ACBS, authored by CompACT co-author n.moghaddam, https://contextualscience.org/comprehensive_assessment_acceptance_commitment_therapy_processes_compact (fetched 2026-09-10; body also mirrored at /book/export/html/16491, sha256 a25e5dd0957275c1713572b4495051f6c422bbe3d85c094211620af9a36408dd) -- states: "The CompACT is free to use for clinical and research purposes: we have attached the CompACT response form and a scoring calculator below." That is a use grant SCOPED BY PURPOSE, not a fitness disclaimer: it grants clinical/research use and grants nothing else, and the attachments carrying the form are themselves gated ("This page contains attachments restricted to ACBS members. Please join or login with your ACBS account."). It is the same shape as the Heartland Forgiveness Scale clause already ruled BLOCK in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv on 2026-09-10 ("If you want to use the HFS for research or clinical purposes, and you will not profit directly from use of the HFS, you may use the HFS" -- blocked because a conditional use grant reserves a right), and it is the hexaco.org free-but-restricted shape that irw#1945 widened the trigger to cover. IRW redistributes, so "our own use is research" is not a defence. THE DEPOSIT LICENCE DOES NOT LAUNDER IT: the OSF project osf.io/cwjxq is CC BY 4.0 and the Czech questionnaire PDF is openly downloadable, but the 2026-09-08 ruling is that the originator's terms govern and that a translation is a derivative of the restricted instrument, so the Czech wording is covered by the English CompACT's terms. THE BLOCK IS EFFECTIVE: the response table's item codes (VA1, OE2R, BA3R ...) carry only subscale letter + item number + reverse flag, no wording, so withholding item text actually withholds the instrument (contrast irw#2101/#2123). HONEST CAVEAT / ESCALATION: this clause is softer than HFS's -- it names no fee, no permission requirement, no explicit non-commercial or no-redistribution term, and "free" plausibly reads as a fee waiver rather than a purpose limit. It is the genuinely ambiguous case SKILL.md says to escalate rather than decide, resolved here in the direction Ben set ("err on the side of not having things"). CompACT has NO row in instrument_rights_register.csv; one is owed, and this agent deliberately did not write the shared register. WHAT WAS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so an unblocked retry is cheap: OSF file CompACT(CZ).pdf (osf.io/download/avrzq/, sha256 a74f9b8e76f39064850b0660f2f27907be97187a8add56e4c6dde2dd2ebcfa4f) carries the full administered Czech instrument -- 23 items numbered 1-23, instructions, and all seven anchors labelled (0 Vubec nesouhlasim ... 6 Uplne souhlasim), matching the live resp set 0-6 exactly; its printed subscale key (Otevrenost vuci zkusenosti 2R,4R,6R,8R,11R,13,15R,18R,20,22; Vedome chovani 3R,9R,12R,16R,19R; Hodnotne jednani 1,5,7,10,14,17,21,23) reproduces the live item codes' subscale letters, numbers and R flags at all 23/23 positions, so mapping_basis would have been paper_explicit with a 23/23 code-key match and text_source study_materials (Czech base fields, English CompACT in the _translated columns). RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry right now reaches the same verdict; the source is fully in hand and the block is a rights determination, not an access failure. What would change it: a ruling from Ben (or a register row) reading "free to use for clinical and research purposes" as a bare fee waiver rather than a stated use restriction, or the rights holder restating the terms.

note: RIGHTS CHECKED FIRST. The DASS is distributed by the Psychology Foundation of Australia at www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/; its FAQ (http://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/DASSFAQ.htm, sha256 a4800f9439e4828d57c4bcd243e4a848b50c404740cae05d4990c2a77bd638b5, fetched 2026-09-10) states "The DASS questionnaire is public domain, and so permission is not needed to use it" and "The DASS questionnaires and scoring key may be downloaded from the DASS website and copied without restriction". That page also carries "it is not permissible to sell the DASS scales themselves to another person" -- a bar on reselling the questionnaire as a product, stated next to an explicit public-domain declaration, not a licence condition reserving a right over reproduction; IRW does not sell the scale, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears. The FAQ additionally governs the TRANSLATION used here: "The only restriction on carrying out a translation is that the translated version, like the original English DASS, must be public domain" and "By posting their translation on the website, translators are making it publicly available, so you do NOT need to obtain their permission to use it." Same verdict as falih_2026_dass21 (batch_031) and neurodegenerative_huizinga_2019_dass (batch_116). LANGUAGE/TEXT: administered in Czech. The paper's Measures section states "The Czech version of the DASS-21 was translated and validated by Vilimovsky and Kucera (Kucera et al., 2018)", which is exactly the form the DASS site distributes at Czech/DASS_21_Czech.pdf (sha256 017ae7cd80bed33ca1e2941528810677f30915494ffade426ae46d28375a5311, fetched 2026-09-10) -- so the administered wording is identified by the study itself, not inferred. item_text, option_text and instructions are transcribed verbatim from that PDF (its two-line item wraps joined with a single space, the leading '1.'..'21.' numbering stripped, one trailing space trimmed; nothing else altered, including its own typo at option 1, "Platilo pro nekdy nebo do urcite miry", which is missing 'me'). The _translated columns are the publisher's official English DASS21 (Download files/Dass21.pdf, sha256 8644cc86534d397e371985d5b25422ba76c4cdae0a5aed8f1a4453c17a5cd393), i.e. the parallel English form rather than a translation of the shipped Czech -- several Vilimovsky items are non-literal renderings (item 8 Czech reads "I felt that I was tense and nervous" against the English "I felt that I was using a lot of nervous energy"). Neither the OSF deposit (osf.io/cwjxq holds exactly two files, Dataset.csv and CompACT(CZ).pdf -- the latter is the CompACT instrument only, no DASS) nor the paper reproduces any DASS wording, hence the instrument site. MAPPING: data/ptacek2023_compact.py melts the deposit's Dataset.csv columns S1, A2, D3, ... D21 BY NAME (DASS21_COLS), so the IRW code IS the source column name and nothing positional can shift. Tying code number n to DASS-21 item n is nonetheless an inference from the instrument's published item order (the source CSV carries no wording), hence paper_order. VERIFIED AGAINST DATA: the paper's Table 4 publishes Mean/SD/Skewness/Kurtosis for the raw Depression, Anxiety and Stress sums in this same N=299 sample; summing the seven items each code's letter assigns reproduces all twelve moments to 2 dp (D 7.023/5.757/0.741/-0.451 vs 7.02/5.76/0.74/-0.45; A 5.050/5.026/1.203/0.747 vs 5.05/5.03/1.20/0.75; S 9.411/4.961/0.294/-0.628 vs 9.41/4.96/0.29/-0.63), against a median worst-block deviation of 2.45 for random 7/7/7 partitions of the same items. That pins the subscale partition and the raw 0-3 direction, not the order within a subscale -- PARTIAL, see verify_ptacek2023_dass21.R. STEP 3b: live data is 21 items x resp 0-3 with codes whose letters give the canonical DASS-21 D/A/S partition, so the table is the DASS-21 and not one of the battery's siblings (CompACT, AAQ-II, SWLS).
